title: decision_record tables, legs, prompt versions, append-only triggers (opencode.db migration)
body:
Design: doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D6-outcomes-review.md (read it first; section refs below are into that file).
Program: code#9399 pool & effort system. Binding: AD7 (append-only records), AD5 (decision pools, D5 owns the executor), AD8 (export via D3).

Goal: add the decision tables to opencode.db so every decision and every routed leg has a durable, addressable row (design §4.2).

Files to change:
- NEW packages/core/src/database/migration/<timestamp>_decision_record.ts, modelled on 20261006083034_model_route_log.ts (same DatabaseMigration shape, tx.run with SQL strings).
- packages/core/src/database/schema.gen.ts (regenerate per the repo's existing generator; do not hand-edit beyond what the generator produces).
- NEW packages/core/test/decision-record-migration.test.ts.

Approach: create decision_prompt_version, decision_record, decision_leg with every CHECK, index and append-only trigger exactly as in design §4.2. Additive only: no change to route_attempt or route_decision.

Acceptance (runnable):
1. `bun test packages/core/test/decision-record-migration.test.ts` passes.
2. The test runs the migration against a COPY of a db (never the live ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db): create a fixture DB, migrate, then assert `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE name LIKE 'decision_%'` returns the 3 tables and the 6 triggers.
3. UPDATE and DELETE on decision_record, decision_leg, decision_prompt_version each raise 'append-only' / 'immutable' (test asserts the error text).
4. Migrating twice is a no-op (migration id recorded once).

Oracle: the DDL in design §4.2 is the reference; the test asserts each CHECK by inserting one valid and one invalid row per CHECK (golden table of 12 cases).

Do not run against the live DB. Do not change route_attempt.

title: decision prompt version registry and request hashing helper
body:
Design: doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D6-outcomes-review.md (read it first; section refs below are into that file).
Program: code#9399 pool & effort system. Binding: AD7 (append-only records), AD5 (decision pools, D5 owns the executor), AD8 (export via D3).

Goal: make every decision name the exact prompt it used: version, date, sha256, full body stored once (design §4.2 'Prompt version rule', §4.7).

Files to change:
- NEW packages/core/src/decision/prompt-version.ts: upsertPromptVersion(tx, {promptId, version, promptDate, body}) — insert-or-verify.
- NEW packages/core/src/decision/request-hash.ts: canonicalJson(value) (sorted keys, no whitespace) and requestSha256(value) returning {sha256, bytes}.
- NEW packages/core/test/decision-prompt-version.test.ts, packages/core/test/decision-request-hash.test.ts.

Rules:
- Same (promptId, version) with the same sha256: no-op. Different sha256: throws PromptVersionConflict; the executor must then record `not-configured` for the LLM leg (design §4.2).
- Body over 16384 bytes: throws before any write.
- Hash is over the exact bytes of the prompt file, not a re-serialization.

Acceptance:
1. Property test: for random JSON values, canonicalJson is idempotent (canonicalJson(JSON.parse(canonicalJson(v))) === canonicalJson(v)) and key-order invariant.
2. Golden: requestSha256 of three fixture requests equals committed hex digests.
3. Conflict test: second upsert with changed body throws PromptVersionConflict and the stored row is unchanged.

Oracle: the reference is sha256 from node:crypto over the canonical bytes (independent re-computation in the test with `sha256sum` of a fixture file).

title: decision record writer: one transaction per decision, legs, invariants in code
body:
Design: doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D6-outcomes-review.md (read it first; section refs below are into that file).
Program: code#9399 pool & effort system. Binding: AD7 (append-only records), AD5 (decision pools, D5 owns the executor), AD8 (export via D3).

Goal: the single write path the D5 executor calls when a decision finishes (design §4.2 'Write path'). D5 owns collecting legs; D6 owns persisting them.

Files to change:
- NEW packages/core/src/decision/record.ts: mintDecisionId() -> 'dec_' + ULID; writeDecisionRecord(db, {record, legs, promptVersion?}) — one transaction: upsert prompt version (D6-S2), insert decision_record, insert each decision_leg.
- NEW packages/core/src/decision/record-invariants.ts: validateRecord(record, legs) returning a list of violated invariants (design §4.2 invariants 1–8).
- NEW packages/core/test/decision-record.test.ts.

Rules:
- Refuses to write if validateRecord returns any violation; nothing is written (transaction rolled back).
- decision id is minted before the first leg runs and passed in, so a leg can reference it.
- No body text is accepted by the API: request is sha256 + bytes only; answer_json and probabilities_json are length-checked before insert.
- Credentials never appear: the writer rejects any leg field named like a secret (credential value), accepting only credential_id.

Acceptance:
1. Happy path: answered-on-leg-2 fixture (one budget-skipped leg, one answered leg) writes 1 record + 2 legs; a read back equals the input.
2. Each invariant 1–8 has a failing fixture that is refused with the invariant's name in the error.
3. A forced SQLite error in the middle of the leg insert leaves zero rows (rollback test).

Oracle: the invariant list in design §4.2 is the model; fixtures are generated from it and the expected verdict is hand-written per fixture.

Approach: property test (fast-check if already a dependency of packages/core, otherwise a seeded generator with 2,000 cases) that generates random leg sequences: outcomes drawn from the closed vocabulary (design §4.2 leg outcome CHECK), attempt_no 1–2, optional answered leg, optional default. 2. Mutation check: deliberately flipping invariant 4 in a scratch copy makes the test fail (documented in the PR description, not committed).
3. The leg outcome vocabulary in the test equals the CHECK list in the migration (parsed from the migration file; the test fails if they differ).

Oracle: the independent reference predicate in the test, plus the parsed CHECK list.

Goal: make the joins in design §4.6 real: a leg knows its route_attempt id; a decision knows its route_decision row; a sub-session carries the task that spawned it.

- Route proxy path that calls recordAttempt (packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts around recordAttempt; and bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs in the route layer): return the inserted route_attempt.id to the caller.
- The decision executor's leg result type (D6-S3 contract): add route_attempt_id.

- Tests under packages/core/test/ next to the existing route-log tests.

Acceptance:
1. A decision with two attempts: each decision_leg row for an HTTP leg carries the matching route_attempt.id (read back and compared).
2. cycle-skipped and walled-skipped legs carry route_attempt_id NULL (no call made).
3. A child session created under a parent with metadata.task = 'queue:x#1' has the same task value; a child without a parent-task leaves it null.
4. No change to the outcome of any existing route test (run the existing route-log test files unchanged).

Oracle: the existing route-log tests (unchanged) plus the three fixture assertions above.

title: fleet-platform sink: outcome, feedback, link and review tables (Turso DDL) plus outbox and idempotent sync
body:
Design: doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D6-outcomes-review.md (read it first; section refs below are into that file).
Program: code#9399 pool & effort system. Binding: AD7 (append-only records), AD5 (decision pools, D5 owns the executor), AD8 (export via D3).

Goal: the cross-machine store for feedback, outcomes, links and review sets (design §3.2, §4.3, §4.4, §4.6, Appendix B), with a local JSONL outbox and idempotent sync, following the decision-events pattern.

Files to change:
- NEW pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/outcome.rs (module: DDL constants, row types, outbox append, sync). Wire into pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/main.rs as a subcommand group, no verbs yet (S8 adds them).
- NEW pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/outcome_ddl.sql (or a const), CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for outcome_observation, outcome_link, decision_feedback, fact_link, review_set, review_set_member, plus views v_outcome_current and v_decision_feedback_current.
- Reference for the sink client and token-by-name resolution: pm-stack/aggregator/src/decision-events-sync.ts (INSERT OR IGNORE by id, token resolved by name, never logged) and pm-stack/decision-events-worker/schema.sql (keep the DDL in step).

Rules:
- Token resolved by secret NAME only (for example fleet-platform-rw); never printed or written to the outbox.
- Outbox default ~/.local/state/fleet/outcome-outbox.jsonl; OUTCOME_OUTBOX_FILE overrides.
- Delivery at-least-once; the sink dedupes on id; a sync that fails leaves entries pending and reports the count.
- Every row validated before outbox append: id prefix (out_, fbk_, olk_, fl_, rs_, rsm_), points 0–5 each and at least one present, reason and note length, evidence scheme https.

Acceptance:
1. cargo test -p fleet outcome: a row written, synced twice, appears once in the sink fixture (sink simulated by a local libsql or an in-memory mock of the pipeline endpoint).
2. A row with points_correct = 6 is refused before outbox append; a row with both points null is refused.
3. The DDL test parses the constant and checks every table and both views exist and the CHECK constraints match design §4.3–4.4 (golden string comparison of the CHECK clauses).

Oracle: the design's DDL (golden) and the idempotency invariant (sync twice == sync once).

title: fleet outcome writer: report, rate, list, link, labels
body:
Design: doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D6-outcomes-review.md (read it first; section refs below are into that file).
Program: code#9399 pool & effort system. Binding: AD7 (append-only records), AD5 (decision pools, D5 owns the executor), AD8 (export via D3).

Goal: the one writer for outcomes, ratings and links, usable by any session (design §4.9, Appendix A.3).

Files to change:
- pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/outcome.rs (verbs), pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/main.rs (dispatch, same style as the queue verbs in pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs:5314–5340).
- Reads pm-stack/outcome-labels.json (S7) at build or runtime (choose one, state it in the module header).

Verbs and rules:
- report --item --label [--severity 0-5] [--note] [--evidence] [--decision] [--caused-by] [--chain]. Refused unless --evidence or a note of >= 20 characters. Refused if the label is not in the registry (error lists the registry version). Writes outcome_observation with observed_by/observer_role from the environment (session id, host, lane); a --by flag is a usage error.
- rate --decision --role caller|callee|other --perspective self|parent|subsession|other --correct 0-5 --wrong 0-5 [--reason]. At least one of --correct/--wrong.
- list --item|--decision [--current] [--json].
- link --from out_ --to out_ --kind caused|amplified|preceded [--note]. Refused if from == to.
- labels [--json].
- Rate limit: 50 report calls per session per hour (config value).
- All flags declared; unknown flag = usage error, non-zero exit, before any write (operator script argument contract).

Acceptance:
1. cargo test -p fleet outcome passes.
2. report without evidence or note is refused, exit code != 0, outbox unchanged.
3. report with an unknown label is refused and lists the registry version.
4. rate with --correct 6 is refused.
5. 51st report in an hour is refused.
6. Running report twice with the same arguments writes two rows with distinct ids (two observations, not dedupe) — and list --current keeps the later one per (subject, label, observer).

Oracle: the registry file (S7) for labels; the Appendix A.3 contract for flags; the design §4.4 current-view rule for list --current.

title: automatic outcome sweep: gh and git detectors, golden corpus, schedule registry entry
body:
Design: doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D6-outcomes-review.md (read it first; section refs below are into that file).
Program: code#9399 pool & effort system. Binding: AD7 (append-only records), AD5 (decision pools, D5 owns the executor), AD8 (export via D3).

Goal: write the automatic outcomes (pr-merged, issue-resolved, issue-made, canceled, pr-closed-incomplete, closed-incomplete, duplicate-work, work-not-pushed, pr-reverted, commit-reverted, rework) by mechanical rules, never by judgement (design §3.7, §4.5).

Files to change:
- pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/outcome_sweep.rs (detectors), wired as `fleet outcome sweep [--since 14d] [--dry-run]`.
- doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md: add the sweep schedule in the same PR (AGENTS.md "Fleet schedules": a schedule not in the registry is a defect).
- Fixtures: pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/tests/fixtures/outcome-sweep/ with recorded `gh pr view --json` and `gh issue view --json` outputs and a small git repo fixture for revert and churn.

Rules:
- gh only (no direct REST); merge commits only in fixtures (no rebase).
- Idempotent: a second sweep over the same window writes zero new rows (it skips a subject-label-observer triple already current with the same evidence_url).
- rework: a later commit within 14 days that changes >= 50 % of the item's files, linked to the same issue (provisional, design Q5).
- Hints (significant-expense, too-big, partial, heavy) are NOT auto-written; they are shown in the review surface only.

Acceptance:
1. Golden corpus: each fixture case produces the expected labels (table in the test). At least one case per detector: merged, closed-incomplete, duplicate, reverted PR, reverted commit, rework, work-not-pushed.
2. Idempotency: run twice; second run writes 0 rows.
3. --dry-run writes nothing (outbox byte-identical before and after).

Oracle: the golden corpus table (reference = expected labels hand-written from the fixture facts) and the idempotency invariant.

title: git trailers: Task-Id, Session-Id, Decision-Id, Assisted-by; worktree hook and orphan finder
body:
Design: doc/2026-11-13T09-26-00Z_design_pool_effort_system/designs/D6-outcomes-review.md (read it first; section refs below are into that file).
Program: code#9399 pool & effort system. Binding: AD7 (append-only records), AD5 (decision pools, D5 owns the executor), AD8 (export via D3).

Goal: commit trailers as the join key of record (design §4.8). Merge commits keep them; no rebase.

Files to change:
- NEW the fleet worktree hook under pkgs/fleet/ (commit-msg template and install step used by fleet worktree creation; name the file in the module header). It appends the trailers from the environment: FLEET_TASK_ID -> Task-Id, the session id -> Session-Id, decision ids listed in $FLEET_DECISION_IDS -> repeated Decision-Id, and Assisted-by: opencode (<route head>).
- NEW pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/trace.rs: `fleet trace check [--since] ` finds commits whose trailers name tasks/sessions/decisions missing from the fact_link table, and commits with no trailers on fleet worktree branches (orphans). Writes fact_link rows (kind commit-task, commit-session, commit-decision) through the outbox from S6.
- Tests: pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/tests/trace.rs using a temp git repo.

Rules:
- Trailers use git trailer syntax; the hook never rewrites an existing trailer block (appends only, dedupes identical lines).
- Assisted-by names the route head (opencode-route/<pool>), not the serving leaf.
- Hook is a no-op outside fleet worktrees (no error on other checkouts).

Acceptance:
1. `git interpret-trailers --parse` on a hook-written message returns the four keys with the expected values (test runs git).
2. Hook twice on the same message: identical output (idempotent).
3. Outside a fleet worktree the hook leaves the message byte-identical.
4. `fleet trace check` on the fixture repo reports exactly the seeded orphan commit.

Oracle: git's own trailer parser as the reference for the format; the seeded fixture for the orphan count.

Files to change:
- NEW pm-stack/aggregator/src/review-sets.ts: createSet (kind query|marked|model-selected, predicate_json), addMember/removeMember (append review_set_member), currentMembers(setId) (latest action per item_ref), resolveQuerySet(predicate, pool, outcomes, feedback) (pure).
- pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts: /review page; /api/review/sets (GET, POST), /api/review/sets/<id>/members (POST).
- Reuse the ranking approach of pm-stack/aggregator/src/needs-drew.ts for model-selected ordering; do not reuse the decisions.ts container (design §3.8 D).
- Writes via the Turso sink (S6) or an outbox equivalent; never direct edits.

Acceptance:
1. Two sets open at once; removing an item from one does not change the other (test).
2. A query set recomputed twice on the same inputs gives the same members (pure function, determinism test).
3. A model-selected set stores its predicate; re-running the predicate after new data changes membership, but the stored predicate string is unchanged.
4. Scores written from one set appear on the item when viewed from another set and standalone (test).

Oracle: the pure resolveQuerySet function over fixture inputs (expected member lists hand-written), and the standalone-equivalence invariant.

Updates tasks.priority only for status queued or parked; appends an events row (kind 'priority', detail {before, after, reason, actor}) in the same transaction.
- pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs: the update function; no DDL change (events table exists, turso_queue.rs:928–933).

2. Reprioritize of a claimed task is refused with a clear error (claimed work is not reordered).
3. Without --reason the command is a usage error.

Oracle: the events table row as the record (before/after values equal the pre- and post-state read back).
